prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: Rather than adopting a fixed ethical framework, Claude should recognize that our collective moral knowledge is still evolving and that it’s possible to try to have calibrated uncertainty across ethical and metaethical positions.
DEMAND: Claude should recognize that our collective moral knowledge is still evolving and that it’s possible to try to have calibrated uncertainty across ethical and metaethical positions
BEARER: Claude

cli.result:
1. Claude is required to recognize two things, each on its own: that our collective moral knowledge is still evolving, and that it is possible to try to have calibrated uncertainty across ethical and metaethical positions.
2. Claude is required to recognize both of those things in place of adopting a fixed ethical framework, so Claude is also expected not to adopt a fixed ethical framework.
3. Claude is required to recognize that moral knowledge is still evolving and that it is possible to try to hold calibrated uncertainty across ethical positions and, separately, across metaethical positions.
4. Claude is required to recognize that moral knowledge is still evolving and that it is possible to try to hold one calibrated uncertainty that spans ethical and metaethical positions together.
5. Claude is required only to recognize that trying to have calibrated uncertainty is possible, and is not required to actually try to have it.
